doc.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Failed New Orleans parade and wagon bands
summary: Parade drumming plans with Chris Tyle derailed when the leader played 'The Saints' too fast; Disneyland wagon parades and Kid Ory.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Gee I wonder if those bands ever do the wagon thing anymore, where they put the band on the wagon and they go out?
Well they used to do that to advertise where they were playing.
That’s where the phrase “on the wagon” came from.

With the trombone hanging over the back. I’d love to play a job like that. I got a chance to play a parade down there, and for weeks, and this fellow Chris, who is also a fine drummer, we were going to play drums, bass drum and snare drum. We studied Bunk’s Brass Band and the Eureka Brass Band, and we got all our sequence of parade beats down ready to go, and couldn’t wait, oh boy, finally we were going to play a real parade in New Orleans. And we got down the street, literally rubbing our hands and waiting for the leader to give us the cue to bring it in. And he just picked up his clarinet and just started playing “The Saints.” Too fast to march to.
I’ve had one parade since then. It did work. It was a lot more in the tradition. But I’d love to play something like that on a horse drawn wagon or something. Disneyland used to do
that. Their main parade at Disneyland was down Main Street in horse drawn wagons. That’s where I heard Kid Ory play.
